whiteboards.words: Quant's own example, a manufacturer in London paying a supplier in Singapore. Step one, lock. The London bank locks the manufacturer's money the moment it accepts the instruction. Step two, credit. The Singapore bank credits the supplier right away against that lock. Step three, settle. The two banks settle with each other in the next window and the lock is released. No new asset and the money never left the banking system. It was a deposit at a regulated bank the whole way.
